findings.message: Base-case cap rate of 3.07% independently verified (NOI $17,790 / $580,000). Well below the 10% threshold; REJECTED classification is supported.

High-rent scenario ($2,200/mo, evidence range_high) with fixed underwriting expenses yields ~3.89% cap rate; with management scaled to 10% of gross (~$4,290 OpEx) yields ~3.81%. Gross yield at zero expenses is only ~3.72%. No plausible rent within documented comps supports VIABLE.

Independent check: ~$5,523/mo rent needed for 10% cap assuming 10% management and fixed taxes/insurance/maintenance (~$1,650/yr). That is ~3.1× the base rent estimate and ~2.5× evidence range_high ($2,200).

Rent ESTIMATED MEDIUM at $1,800/mo with documented range $1,400–$2,200. Mid-range estimate is not overly optimistic, but price-to-rent ratio ($580k / $1,800/mo ≈ 322×) is incompatible with a 10% unlevered cap rate.
Purchase price VERIFIED HIGH at $580,000 via YapaTree listing. Price anchor is well supported.

HOA/alicuota UNKNOWN (LOW confidence). Underwriting correctly includes $0 for NOI math only and does not assert verified zero. Any confirmed HOA would further compress an already sub-threshold cap rate; does not change REJECTED outcome.

Special assessments UNKNOWN (LOW confidence). Underwriting correctly excludes them from the base expense total rather than asserting zero. Any confirmed assessment would reduce NOI further; does not change REJECTED outcome.
Rental and STR restrictions both UNKNOWN (LOW confidence). LTR-only income path is assumed without bylaws. Restrictions could limit use case but are immaterial given the cap rate gap.
Taxes ESTIMATED LOW at $50/yr pending municipal bill; listing mirrors cite ~$10.78/yr. Even a materially higher predial bill would not close the gap to 10% cap rate.
Expense arithmetic verified: $50 + $400 + $2,160 + $0 + $1,200 = $3,810 OpEx; gross $21,600 − $3,810 = NOI $17,790. Management equals 10% of base rent.
